question: Can a data-trained regression from approximately scale- and boost-invariant jet substructure to jet transverse momentum expose a new factorized particle species, and under what assumptions does that regression become an optimal signal-versus-background classifier?

key_findings.claim: FORCE turns a physics factorization hypothesis into a simple regression anomaly score: predict a high-scale kinematic variable from nominally independent low-scale structure and flag nonconstant predictions.
key_findings.evidence: The paper models both background and signal as separately factorized products P_i(pT)P_i(O). Their mixture induces a conditional dependence even though each component has none. A network trained with mean-squared error estimates E[pT|O]; its output is then used directly as the per-jet anomaly score. In the jet case, O is a seven-element independent subset of normalized energy-flow polynomials, and the same threshold is applied to both jets in an event.

anchors.section: FORCE procedure, EFP normalization, and network setup

key_findings.claim: The optimal-classifier theorem is correct for the stated two-component model, but it is substantially narrower than a general guarantee for factorized anomaly detection.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 7 is a fractional-linear, hence monotone, function of the signal-to-background likelihood ratio only when there is one signal component, one background component, exact within-component independence, and different component means in pT. If the signal and background pT means are equal, the conditional mean is constant even when higher moments differ; with multiple background or signal categories, one scalar conditional mean mixes several likelihood ratios and need not isolate new physics. The paper explicitly notes the equal-mean null case, QCD's quark/gluon admixture, known Standard Model heavy-particle components, and the need to generalize beyond two categories.

key_findings.claim: The realistic study is a useful controlled proof of concept, not an operationally unsupervised search on unknown data.
key_findings.evidence: The benchmark contains one million simulated QCD dijet events and up to 100,000 simulated W-prime-to-XY events, with no pileup or multiple-parton interactions and known truth labels. For the signal-fraction sweep, the authors select exactly 100,000 signal and 100,000 background events using those labels and use label-derived sample weights to emulate each desired fraction. They also state that the full dataset is used for training and acknowledge that statistically independent train and test samples would be preferable. The regression loss itself is label-free, but the reported low-fraction experiment and evaluation are not an end-to-end label-free deployment protocol.

anchors.section: LHC Olympics sample, event selection, and training protocol

key_findings.claim: FORCE approaches the supervised EFP classifier at high signal fraction, but its low-fraction discrimination is highly variable and does not support a broad reliability claim by itself.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 3 reports supervised AUC 0.87 plus or minus 0.00; FORCE gives 0.86 plus or minus 0.02 at fS=0.5, 0.77 plus or minus 0.03 at 0.05, 0.59 plus or minus 0.15 at 0.005, 0.59 plus or minus 0.13 at 0.0005, and 0.56 plus or minus 0.16 at zero signal. Thus the central score at 0.5% is only modestly above random with an uncertainty spanning near-random behavior, while 0.05% is indistinguishable from the no-signal central result. The paper itself warns that initialization and statistical fluctuations dominate as signal becomes rare.

key_findings.claim: The displayed greater-than-five-sigma bumps demonstrate selection power on the injected sample, but they are local, manually selected diagnostics rather than calibrated discovery significances.
key_findings.evidence: At fS=0.005, the uncut W-prime and X excesses are about 2 sigma and the Y excess about 1 sigma; selected FORCE thresholds raise all three above 5 local sigma. The thresholds are explicitly chosen manually to highlight qualitative behavior. Backgrounds are fit outside shaded windows with fifth-order Legendre polynomials, orders two through seven define an uncertainty envelope, and the plots show local residual significance. There is no blinded threshold rule, held-out optimization, look-elsewhere correction, coverage study, nuisance-parameter likelihood, or pseudo-experiment calibration for the quoted peaks.

anchors.section: Figure 9 unshuffled bump hunts across fractions

key_findings.claim: The paper detects meaningful violations of strict factorization, and its shuffled controls do not establish that those violations are negligible in the difficult low-signal regime.
key_findings.evidence: On original samples, a model trained at fS=0 remains nonconstant and obtains AUC 0.56 plus or minus 0.16, which the authors attribute to residual QCD, detector, or off-manifold effects. After separately shuffling pT and O within each truth class to enforce exact factorization, the corresponding AUC is 0.52 plus or minus 0.08. More strikingly, at fS=0.005 the shuffled AUC is 0.72 plus or minus 0.13 versus 0.59 plus or minus 0.15 unshuffled. Similar-looking mass plots therefore do not show that factorization error is small relative to the sought rare-signal effect.

key_findings.claim: EFP normalization reduces measured pT and mass dependence, but the source does not provide the classifier-performance ablation it says it does.
key_findings.evidence: The seven retained EFP combinations divide out energy and angular moments to obtain quasi-scale- and quasi-boost-invariance. Figure 7 compares histogram mutual information under unnormalized, energy-only, angular-only, and full normalization and generally finds the full normalization smallest; finite jet radius prevents exact invariance, and several normalized EFPs retain visible mass dependence. The main text says the supplement shows FORCE performance degrading without normalization, but the supplement reports mutual-information bars rather than an unnormalized-versus-normalized FORCE AUC or significance comparison.

key_findings.claim: The Gaussian control validates the algebra in an ideal setting, while also exposing the sample-complexity collapse expected for rare mixtures.
key_findings.evidence: Independent unit-variance Gaussian signal and background components satisfy the assumed product mixture exactly, with both means shifted from zero to one for signal. The analytic conditional expectation and neural output agree at high fS; Figure 5 gives AUC 0.76 for both supervised and fS=0.5, 0.75 plus or minus 0.00 at 0.05, 0.59 plus or minus 0.09 at 0.005, and 0.50 at 0.0005 and zero. This is a clean theorem check, but it shows that exact factorization alone does not supply enough finite-sample signal at very low fractions.

key_findings.claim: The empirical scope is much smaller than the claimed breadth: one resonant, two-prong simulator benchmark and no direct anomaly-method baseline are evaluated.
key_findings.evidence: All realistic results use the same W-prime-to-XY LHC Olympics development signal, whose 3.5 TeV dijet and 500/100 GeV jet-mass peaks provide strong localized handles. The paper says FORCE need not require a resonance but evaluates no nonresonant signal and notes that another background-estimation method would be required without a bump. It does not compare CWoLa Hunting, ANODE, CATHODE, CURTAINs, density estimation, autoencoders, simple correlation tests, linear regression, boosted trees, or alternate EFP/particle representations; the only performance ceiling is a supervised classifier on the same seven features.

key_findings.claim: The associated code release is inspectable but does not reproduce the paper's reported protocol as checked and contains a broken factorization control.
key_findings.evidence: At r-wynne/FORCE commit 27d743dfc4fcf4356511c774d77d113ce25bb103, the Python scripts compile and notebooks expose preprocessing, regression, plotting, and Gaussian analyses. However, absolute author-local paths and external unversioned Dropbox artifacts are required; there is no environment lock, tests, CI, license, seed control, or included model/result bundle. The paper's main network is three 50-node layers with L2, dropout, and patience 10, whereas the notebooks use three 100-node layers with regularization and dropout commented out, a hard-coded Adam rate, and the sweep helper uses 100 fixed epochs without early stopping. The main Gaussian script uses four 10-node layers, up to 10,000 epochs, and eight models instead of the stated three 100-node layers, 10 epochs, and ten models. Most critically, FORCE.ipynb and sweep.ipynb assign both the purported shuffled EFPs and shuffled pT targets in their original within-class order and apply the same final permutation, preserving rather than destroying their pairing. FORCE.ipynb also computes background jet masses from efps_signal, and the released sweep evaluates predictions on the same selected X used for fitting while averaging ten models into one outer replicate, which cannot produce the displayed across-training standard deviations as written.

anchors.section: Reported main-network setup and code availability
Reported reweighting, testing, and ten-model protocol

method.core_idea: Exploit approximate independence between energy scales: within each physical species, high-scale kinematics and normalized low-scale structure factorize, but mixing species creates a correlation that a conditional-mean regressor can expose.
method.mechanism: Choose a kinematic target pT and quasi-scale-/boost-invariant substructure O. Normalize energy-flow polynomials by energy and angular moments, retain seven independent inputs, and fit an MLP to pT with mean-squared error. Under a two-product-mixture model, the learned conditional mean is a monotone transform of P_S(O)/P_B(O) whenever the component pT means differ. Apply a lower score cut to both leading jets, inspect jet and dijet mass spectra, and estimate smooth backgrounds with sideband Legendre fits. Sweep emulated signal fractions using truth-derived sample weights, repeat training, and compare per-jet ROC curves with a supervised classifier. Use Gaussian and within-class shuffle controls to test the theorem and factorization premise.
assumptions: Signal and background each factorize separately between the selected kinematic target and substructure inputs.
There is effectively one background class and one signal class, or additional classes combine without breaking monotonicity.
Signal and background have different conditional-target means; higher-moment-only changes are not the intended signal.
Normalized EFPs are sufficiently independent of pT despite finite jet radius, running coupling, containment, flavor mixtures, pileup, and detector response.
A nonconstant conditional mean indicates new physics rather than an unmodeled Standard Model component, detector drift, or residual feature leakage.
The selected seven EFPs contain the relevant substructure signal and do not omit anomalies visible only at constituent level or in other observables.
Mean-squared regression and the chosen MLP converge sufficiently close to the population conditional expectation at the available rare-signal sample size.
Training on all data, or overlapping training and evaluation data, does not create a misleading anomaly score through overfitting or memorization.
Label-weighted balanced-sample experiments faithfully predict what training directly on an unknown, naturally imbalanced dataset would do.
Manually selected score thresholds and polynomial sideband fits provide stable background estimates and calibrated local residuals.
The one simulated W-prime-to-XY sample is representative of the broader factorized signal family, including nonresonant cases.
Ten network initializations characterize statistical and optimization uncertainty even without independent data resamples or a full nuisance model.

techniques.role: Separates high-scale kinematics from low-scale substructure within each latent physical category.
Uses MSE regression to estimate E[pT|O] as the anomaly score.
Relates the two-component conditional mean monotonically to the signal/background likelihood ratio.
Represents jet substructure with energy-flow polynomials derived from particle energies and pairwise angles.
Divides out energy and angular moments to reduce scale, boost, pT, and mass correlations.
Emulates prescribed signal fractions from a balanced truth-selected sample using sample weights.
Repeats neural training to characterize initialization sensitivity and average ROC behavior.
Requires both leading jets to exceed the same FORCE score threshold before bump hunting.
Fits smooth jet and dijet backgrounds with Legendre polynomial families outside selected mass windows.
Intends to enforce exact within-class factorization by independently shuffling kinematics and structure.
Measures histogram mutual information under four EFP normalization schemes.
Compares neural regression with an analytic conditional expectation in an exact product-mixture toy model.

evaluations.setting: Exact two-component Gaussian product mixture with one million background samples, varied injected signal fraction, and analytic conditional expectation.
evaluations.metric: Per-sample ROC AUC and agreement between learned and analytic E[pT|O].
evaluations.result: AUC matches the supervised 0.76 at fS=0.5, is 0.75 at 0.05, falls to 0.59 plus or minus 0.09 at 0.005, and reaches random 0.50 at 0.0005 and zero; learned curves visibly approach the analytic conditional mean at high fraction.
evaluations.baseline: An optimal supervised classifier and the closed-form likelihood-ratio transform; no finite-sample statistical test or alternate regressor.

evaluations.setting: LHC Olympics R&D simulation with R=1 anti-kT jets, pT above 1.2 TeV, absolute pseudorapidity below 2.5, seven normalized EFP inputs, and truth-weighted signal fractions.
evaluations.metric: Per-jet signal/background ROC AUC and variation across ten network trainings.
evaluations.result: AUC is 0.86 plus or minus 0.02 at fS=0.5 and 0.77 plus or minus 0.03 at 0.05, but only 0.59 plus or minus 0.15 at 0.005 and 0.59 plus or minus 0.13 at 0.0005, compared with supervised 0.87 and no-signal 0.56 plus or minus 0.16.
evaluations.baseline: A supervised MLP on the same seven EFPs; no CWoLa, density, sideband-generation, autoencoder, boosted-tree, linear, or simple-correlation baseline.

evaluations.setting: Simulated W-prime-to-XY bump hunt at fS=0.005 with the same FORCE threshold applied to both jets and Legendre fits outside jet/dijet signal windows.
evaluations.metric: Mass-spectrum visibility and plotted local residual significance.
evaluations.result: The displayed cuts raise approximately 2-sigma W-prime and X excesses and a 1-sigma Y excess above 5 local sigma, revealing peaks at 3.5 TeV, 500 GeV, and 100 GeV.
evaluations.baseline: No-cut spectrum and polynomial background fits; thresholds are manually selected and there is no global-significance or coverage calibration.

evaluations.setting: Normalization and factorization controls on the LHC Olympics signal and background, including EFP mutual information and within-class shuffled targets.
evaluations.metric: Histogram mutual information with pT/mass, ROC AUC, and qualitative bump preservation.
evaluations.result: Full normalization generally has the lowest measured dependence, but not zero dependence. Exact-factorization shuffling moves fS=0 AUC from 0.56 to 0.52 and fS=0.005 AUC from 0.59 to 0.72, while the mass-plot pattern remains qualitatively similar.
evaluations.baseline: Unnormalized, energy-normalized, angular-normalized, and fully normalized EFPs plus original versus truth-shuffled samples; no classifier AUC ablation across all four normalization choices.

limitations: Author-stated: performance depends on the applicability of factorization and may not transfer to other scenarios.
Author-stated: quark/gluon mixtures, QCD running, partial containment, detector effects, pileup, and known Standard Model heavy particles can create factorization-violating correlations.
Author-stated: sensitivity becomes highly initialization- and fluctuation-dependent at low signal fraction, motivating ensembles.
Author-stated: detector effects may require multidimensional unfolding, and grooming may be needed to improve theoretical factorization.
Author-stated: a nonresonant application still needs a separate background-estimation strategy.
Author-stated: no generic data-driven search can outperform a correctly specified targeted hypothesis test.
Reviewer inference: the likelihood-ratio equivalence fails for equal target means, higher-moment-only differences, and generic multi-component mixtures.
Reviewer inference: the truth-selected, truth-weighted balanced training experiment is not an operational unsupervised protocol for unknown collider data.
Reviewer inference: training and evaluation are not kept statistically independent, and the paper itself notes that an independent split would be preferable.
Reviewer inference: the realistic evidence is one simulated, resonant, two-prong signal with pileup and multiple-parton interactions disabled.
Reviewer inference: no direct anomaly-detector, simple regression, tree, density, or alternative-representation baseline is run on the same protocol.
Reviewer inference: greater-than-five-sigma values are manually selected local residuals without a look-elsewhere correction, blinded selection, nuisance likelihood, or coverage demonstration.
Reviewer inference: mutual-information reduction is not the promised end-to-end unnormalized-versus-normalized FORCE performance ablation.
Reviewer inference: the shuffled low-fraction AUC materially differs from the original result, showing that approximation error can be comparable to the rare-signal effect.
Reviewer inference: the public code has substantial paper/protocol drift and does not provide a one-command, independently seeded reproduction.
failure_modes: A new species has the same mean pT as background but differs in pT variance or tails, making conditional-mean regression blind despite useful dependence.
Quark/gluon composition changes with pT and produces a score variation that mimics a new factorized species.
Known W, Z, Higgs, or top jets appear as the anomaly and obscure a rarer unknown component.
Pileup, detector nonuniformity, calibration drift, trigger thresholds, or jet containment create stronger cross-scale correlations than the signal.
A signal violates factorization internally, so the conditional mean is not monotone in its optimal likelihood ratio.
Several signal or background components induce a nonmonotone scalar conditional mean and collapse distinct categories onto the same score.
The anomaly lies outside the seven retained EFPs or is erased by quasi-invariant normalization and clipping.
The rare component contributes too few effective weighted examples for regression to learn anything beyond initialization noise.
Training on the evaluation events memorizes finite-sample correlations that fail on a fresh run period.
A FORCE selection sculpts a smooth mass spectrum into a local bump through residual mass correlation.
Manual threshold and fit-order selection overstates local significance through uncounted trials.
Polynomial sidebands fail to extrapolate through a signal window or under-cover shape uncertainty after a tight score cut.
The released shuffle code preserves pT/EFP pairing, so a supposed exact-factorization test silently measures the original correlations.
Hard-coded paths, missing model artifacts, unpinned Keras APIs, and absent seeds prevent independent reproduction of the reported curves.
reusable_insights: Treat conditional prediction across nominally independent variable groups as a transparent correlation detector with an explicit physical inductive bias.
State optimality conditions algebraically and test every one: component count, conditional independence, target-moment separation, model convergence, and finite-sample support.
Use a vector of conditional statistics or a conditional density when anomalies may change variance, tails, or multiple latent components rather than only the mean.
Measure factorization closure on background-only control data across run periods, detector regions, flavors, pT bins, pileup, and generator variations before unblinding.
Build shuffled controls with independently permuted indices and unit-test that cross-feature dependence collapses while each marginal is exactly preserved.
Separate train, threshold-tuning, background-fit, and final statistical-evaluation samples, even for label-free objectives.
Distinguish an unsupervised loss from an unsupervised end-to-end experiment; truth-based sampling or weighting belongs only in sensitivity studies.
Pre-register score thresholds and fit families, then calibrate global significance and coverage with background-only pseudo-experiments.
Compare against simple linear and tree regressors, direct correlation tests, CWoLa, density-ratio methods, and sideband generators on the identical inputs and data splits.
Report anomaly-score stability and calibration, not only supervised truth AUC, because real searches do not know the signal labels.
Publish data hashes, environment locks, seeds, model checkpoints, aggregate metrics, and a small deterministic smoke test alongside figure notebooks.
Use factorization residuals as a systematic uncertainty or nuisance model rather than assuming small mutual information is harmless at rare-signal fractions.
open_questions: Can conditional density estimation or learned higher moments retain FORCE's interpretability while detecting equal-mean and multi-component anomalies?
What necessary and sufficient conditions make a vector-valued regression score recover the optimal likelihood ratio for more than two latent categories?
How large can measured factorization violation be before a claimed signal fraction is no longer identifiable?
Can background-only control regions provide a finite-sample certificate or calibrated bound on spurious FORCE score variation?
Does FORCE work on nonresonant signals when evaluated with a complete background-estimation and hypothesis-testing pipeline?
How does it compare with CATHODE, CWoLa Hunting, ANODE, full-phase-space diffusion, DDD, and boosted trees under matched compute and representations?
Do constituent-level equivariant regressors improve sensitivity without reintroducing strong pT or mass leakage?
Can nuisance-aware or adversarial training remove detector and pileup dependence without erasing genuine cross-scale new-physics correlations?
What is the correct global-significance calibration when scanning targets, feature groups, score directions, thresholds, mass windows, and fit families?
How should multiple known Standard Model species be modeled so that rediscovery becomes a validation step rather than a false anomaly?
Does training directly on a naturally imbalanced million-event mixture reproduce the truth-weighted balanced-sample curves on disjoint test data?
Can the public implementation be rebuilt as a declarative, seeded suite whose exact-factorization tests fail automatically if pairings are preserved?

competitive_landscape.title: Classification without labels: Learning from mixed samples in high energy physics
competitive_landscape.difference: CWoLa proves that classifying two mixtures with different class proportions recovers the fully supervised decision boundary without instance labels or known proportions. FORCE replaces the need for two externally defined mixtures with two nominally factorized variable groups inside one sample, but gains much stricter independence and target-mean assumptions.

competitive_landscape.title: Anomaly Detection for Resonant New Physics with Machine Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: CWoLa Hunting learns from a signal mass window versus sidebands and requires localization in one known direction. FORCE can in principle detect a nonresonant factorized species, but its only realistic demonstration is the same kind of resonant dijet benchmark and still relies on a bump fit for statistical interpretation.

competitive_landscape.title: Machine Learning Templates for QCD Factorization in the Search for Physics Beyond the Standard Model
competitive_landscape.difference: This work learns data-driven conditional QCD templates from a background-rich region under a factorization assumption and uses them to predict backgrounds. FORCE instead treats violation of a within-species kinematics/substructure factorization as the anomaly score, avoiding a generator but not producing a complete background estimate for nonresonant use.

competitive_landscape.title: Classifying Anomalies THrough Outer Density Estimation (CATHODE)
competitive_landscape.difference: CATHODE learns a conditional background density in sidebands, samples it in a signal region, and trains a data-versus-background classifier; on the LHC Olympics benchmark it reports near-optimal performance and robustness to feature correlations. It requires a localized signal region and a generative model, whereas FORCE is cheaper and potentially nonresonant but more fragile to factorization leakage.

competitive_landscape.title: Disentangling Quarks and Gluons with CMS Open Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Komiske, Kryhin, and Thaler apply topic-mixture reasoning and ROC-endpoint regression to extract latent quark/gluon categories in unfolded real CMS data; FORCE explicitly credits this as a prior regression route to an optimal classifier. The earlier method uses two observed mixed samples plus reducibility assumptions, while FORCE uses a cross-scale conditional mean in one mixture.

competitive_landscape.title: The Interplay of Machine Learning--based Resonant Anomaly Detection Methods
competitive_landscape.difference: This primary benchmark tests whether resonant anomaly methods select the same background and signal events and finds gains from combining complementary detectors. FORCE presents itself as a complementary assumption class, but does not enter such a matched benchmark; its residuals could be combined with sideband and density scores to reduce method-specific false positives.

competitive_landscape.title: Full Phase Space Resonant Anomaly Detection
competitive_landscape.difference: Buhmann et al. extend sideband-generated backgrounds to variable-length particle clouds and the full event phase space, trading substantially greater modeling and compute for broader representation. FORCE is a seven-feature scalar regression with a clear theorem, but can miss signals outside its hand-selected factorized observables.

competitive_landscape.title: Universal Anomaly Detection at the LHC: Transforming Optimal Classifiers and the DDD Method
competitive_landscape.difference: DDD trains a standard discriminator against synthetically distorted background events and evaluates multiple channels and four-top production, offering a broad nonresonant inductive bias with no factorization theorem. FORCE has a more interpretable physics assumption and analytic optimum, while DDD covers richer event representations and explicitly compares several anomaly baselines.

competitive_landscape.title: Inferring correlated distributions: boosted top jets
competitive_landscape.difference: Alvarez et al. extend Bayesian collider mixture models to correlated within-class observables, using imperfect simulator correlations as priors that data corrects. This directly addresses a central FORCE failure mode at the cost of simulation dependence and a more structured probabilistic model.

competitive_landscape.title: Machine-learning techniques for model-independent searches in dijet final states
competitive_landscape.difference: The CMS Collaboration reports anomaly-detection methods used with 13 TeV collision data, compares their sensitivity, and demonstrates model-agnostic recovery of boosted top jets. It supplies the detector-systematics and real-data benchmark absent from FORCE's Delphes-only study; a mature FORCE validation should be tested within this kind of experimental workflow.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Cross-scale factorization supplies a physically interpretable anomaly-detection inductive bias: regressing kinematics from invariant substructure in a mixed dataset yields the optimal new-physics classifier under strict factorization and reveals percent-level signals without simulation labels or a resonance requirement.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The two-component derivation is exact, an analytic Gaussian test matches it, and the LHC Olympics W-prime-to-XY benchmark approaches the supervised seven-EFP classifier at large signal fractions. A dual-jet FORCE selection makes injected 3.5 TeV, 500 GeV, and 100 GeV resonances visually prominent and raises their plotted local residuals above five sigma at fS=0.005.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The genuinely novel contribution is the conditional-mean implementation of a factorized-mixture detector, with a rare and valuable explicit theorem connecting a physics assumption to an anomaly score. It is not a general optimal anomaly detector: equal means, multiple components, within-class correlations, detector effects, and finite rare-signal samples break the result. The one truth-weighted simulated benchmark, manually selected local significances, absence of matched anomaly baselines, and materially inconsistent public notebooks prevent the evidence from establishing an operational unsupervised search or reliable sub-percent sensitivity. The strongest follow-up is a multi-statistic or conditional-density FORCE family with measured factorization residuals, disjoint samples, global statistical calibration, real-data closure, and executable tests of every control.

reviewer_notes: Read all 17 extracted pages, including the five-page main article, six reference pages, and six-page supplement. Rendered and visually inspected every page and closely audited Figures 1-10 and Table I; exact AUC legend values, local-significance labels, normalization bars, and shuffled/original bump panels were read from the rendered source. Current primary arXiv, publisher, citation-index, and experimental sources were checked through 2026-08-23. The hashed source is arXiv v2, updated 2024-08-29 as the approximate Physical Review D version; the final article is Phys. Rev. D 110, 055012, published 2024-09-09, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevD.110.055012. Audited https://github.com/r-wynne/FORCE at commit 27d743dfc4fcf4356511c774d77d113ce25bb103: all ordinary Python files pass syntax compilation, but no full training was attempted because the release depends on external large data/results, author-local absolute paths, and an unpinned legacy stack. The audit inspected all code cells without notebook binary outputs and directly verified the network/protocol drift, missing independent shuffled indices in FORCE.ipynb and sweep.ipynb, signal-EFP typo for background jet masses, same-X fitting/evaluation path, single outer replicate, absent seeds/tests/CI/license/environment, and five-commit repository history ending 2023-12-03.
